item.title: Swedish Fika Calendar: Why Swedes eat cake on the first Thursday of March
item.description: Hej and welcome to the latest instalment of The Local's Fika Calender, where we guide you through the most important cake, pastry and other food-related days in the Swedish year.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: prinsesstårta
item.description: You've no doubt seen these domed, bright green cream cakes at your local bakery, but what's the story behind Sweden's princess cakes (and what's the difference between a paj, a tårta and a kaka, anyway)?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Sweden's inflation rate falls faster than expected, first repatriation grants set to be handed out, and Swedes' trust in Nato falls – but they still love Systembolaget. Here's the latest news.

item.title: Sweden to hand out first new repatriation grants
item.description: Sweden’s Migration Agency has for the first time approved applications for the government’s controversial 350,000 kronor “repatriation grant” – money handed out to refugees who wish to return to their home countries, a scheme criticised by the government’s own inquiry.

item.title: Does Sweden need an 'integration amnesty' to stop deportations?
item.description: Few positions are more central on Sweden’s political right than the one Fredrik Kopsch holds as chief economist at Timbro. But as he launches a new book on deportations, Utvisad, which calls for an amnesty for integrated foreigners, he says his liberal views feel increasingly at out of place.

item.title: Spring has now arrived in Stockholm
item.description: It may not feel like it quite yet, but spring has now officially arrived in Stockholm, with winter officially over for the entire southern half of the country.

item.title: Pollution exposure in Europe linked to mental health problems
item.description: Environmental pollution is linked to several mental health disorders in Europe, the European Environment Agency (EEA) has warned, arguing that enforcing legislation would result in Europeans being both less depressed and less anxious.

item.title: NEW: The Local’s self-paced Swedish course
item.description: Due to popular demand The Local's self-paced online Swedish course for beginners is back, designed to make learning flexible and practical.

item.title: Sweden Democrat leader calls for freeze on teen deportations
item.description: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has called for the country’s controversial ‘teen deportations’ to be suspended with immediate effect until a solution has been found.

item.title: Swedish intelligence warns of increased Middle East war fallout
item.description: A top Swedish intelligence official has warned of increased threats against American and Israeli interests, as well as Iranian dissidents, in Sweden because of the war in the Middle East.
